question: What is the product formed when zinc and sulphuric acid react?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Zinc sulphate**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• When zinc reacts with sulphuric acid, it undergoes a chemical reaction to form zinc sulphate and hydrogen gas.
 
• The balanced chemical equation for this reaction is: Zn + H₂SO₄ → ZnSO₄ + H₂.
 
• Zinc sulphate is an inorganic compound with the formula ZnSO₄.
 
• This reaction is a typical example of a metal reacting with an acid to produce a salt and hydrogen gas.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Zinc (Zn)**

 
 
• Zinc is a transition metal with the atomic number 30.
 
• It is commonly used in galvanizing to prevent rusting of steel and iron.
 
• Zinc is also an essential trace element necessary for human health.
 
 
 
• **Sulphuric Acid (H₂SO₄)**
 
 
• It is a strong mineral acid with highly corrosive properties.
 
• Sulphuric acid is used in a variety of industrial processes such as fertilizer production, oil refining, and chemical synthesis.
 
• It is also known as oil of vitriol.
 
 
 
• **Chemical Reactions**
 
 
• A chemical reaction involves the transformation of reactants into products.
 
• Reactions are often accompanied by the release or absorption of energy.
 
• They can be categorized into different types such as synthesis, decomposition, single replacement, and double replacement reactions.
 
 
 
• **Safety Precautions**
 
 
• When handling sulphuric acid, it is crucial to wear appropriate safety gear including gloves, goggles, and lab coats due to its highly corrosive nature.
 
• Ensure proper ventilation when conducting chemical reactions to avoid inhaling harmful gases.
 
• Always add acid to water, not water to acid, to prevent exothermic reactions that can cause splashing.
